title: Al-Muntaqim, the Requiter
hook: the Requiter, who makes right every wrong
tomorrow: forgive, or erase? why one night's prayer asks for the second.

segments.voice: Yesterday, At-Tawwab, the Ever-Relenting, who turns toward the one who turns back. The line: he turns to me. Today, the harder question: what about the wrong nobody ever turns back from?
screen: `HE TURNS TO ME.` → `AND THE ONE WHO NEVER TURNS?`

segments.voice: Somewhere in a camera roll there's a screenshot kept as proof: the unfair message, the thing someone said, saved for a reckoning that never quite comes. Now a day the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, remembered as one of the hardest of his life. Tradition places it after the town of Ta'if turned him away. He walks off, overwhelmed with grief, and doesn't come back to himself until he's far down the road. He looks up. A cloud is shading him, and in it is the angel Gabriel. And Gabriel has brought someone with an offer.
screen: `THE SCREENSHOT KEPT AS PROOF.` → `TURNED AWAY.` → `A CLOUD, AND AN OFFER.`

segments.voice: It's the angel of the mountains. In the hadith in Bukhari, he greets the Prophet and says: if you wish, I will bring the two mountains together on them. One word, and the people who turned him away are gone. He says no. He says he hopes that from their children, God will bring people who worship God alone. His wife Aisha said, in another report, that he never took revenge for his own sake. So how does that sit with today's Name? Al-Muntaqim, the Requiter. The Qur'an calls Allah, in Pickthall's words, "Mighty, Able to Requite (the wrong)." And it promises: "And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then, And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight will see it then." Here's the turn. Because no wrong is forgotten by God, the Prophet didn't have to bring the mountains down himself. The reckoning was held somewhere safer than his own anger, which left his hands free to hope for those people's children. That's the line to tell a friend tonight: in this story, the one who was wronged is offered revenge, and spends the offer on his enemies' future. Al-Muntaqim isn't a God who loses His temper. It's the promise that nothing done in the dark just disappears.
screen: `THE ANGEL OF THE MOUNTAINS.` · `HE SAYS NO.` · `AN ATOM'S WEIGHT WILL BE SEEN.` · `THE RECKONING HELD SOMEWHERE SAFER.` · then, large: `NO WRONG FORGOTTEN.`

segments.voice: On a scrap of paper, write a few words for one wrong you're still holding; no names needed. Fold it once and set it down beside you, out of your hand. For the sit, let it stay there: not erased, not forgotten, just no longer yours alone to carry.
Al-Muntaqim. The Requiter, who makes right every wrong, so the one who was wronged doesn't have to carry the mountains.
Hold on to this one: no wrong forgotten, not by Him, so your hands are free for something else. That's fifteen fifty-five.

screen: `DAY 1555 COUNTS.` → `NAME 81 OF 99 · YEAR FIVE, 129 OF 365.` → `TOMORROW: FORGIVE, OR ERASE? WHY ONE NIGHT'S PRAYER ASKS FOR THE SECOND.`

howItsDone: When wronged, some Muslims say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, Allah is enough for us, still seeking fair redress while leaving the final reckoning to God.

match.prompt: the offer on the road — tap the pairs.

myth: Al-Muntaqim means God gets even the way an angry person does
the Name means nothing done is lost or left unanswered; it isn't a temper.
in the hadith, the Prophet turned down an angel's offer to destroy the people who turned him away
he hoped God would bring believers from their children instead.
leaving a wrong to God means pretending it never happened
the Qur'an says even an atom's weight of ill will be seen.

fork.setup: someone posts a cruel edited photo of your friend. your friend has a worse one ready to post back. what fits today's story?
options: post it; the Requiter wants every wrong answered, so answer it.
report the photo, skip the counter-post, leave the payback to God.
do nothing at all; even reporting it is a kind of revenge.
fork.reveal: offered the mountains, the Prophet said no. fair steps are fine; the payback belongs to the One who forgets no wrong.

original.note: Arabic: the Requiter, from the traditional list of the Names; the Qur'an calls Allah 'Able to Requite (the wrong)'.

trapdoor: what you thought: a God who gets even.
what it means: the One who makes right every wrong, so nothing done in the dark just disappears.
what a scholar hears: the Qur'an's phrase dhu intiqam, owner of requital (3:4), read beside the Prophet who, Aisha said, never avenged himself (Bukhari 6126).

chat.says: someone tagged our mural overnight. dad just shrugged and made coffee. i want them found and PAID back.
options: Report it, sure. But the payback isn't yours to carry. God forgets no wrong.
Let it go right now. Wanting a wrong made right at all shows weak faith.
Find them yourself and make them pay. Leaving it to God is just giving up.
chat.meaning: Offered revenge, the Prophet said no. Al-Muntaqim makes right every wrong, so the one who was wronged doesn't carry it alone.

notes: 2026-10-15 v3 (recipe v3), story shape: one scene (the angel of the mountains), mid-action; the teach answers the cliffhanger.

Bukhari 3231 / Muslim 1795 paraphrased: the hadith speaks of the day he presented himself to Ibn 'Abd Yalil and left in grief; linking it to Ta'if is the standard reading, given as 'tradition places it'. The stoning details from the sira are deliberately left out. Gentle for parents: the scene is grief and an offer of destruction, declined.
Bukhari 6126 (Aisha: he never took revenge for himself unless God's limits were violated) paraphrased without the exception; confirm the framing is fair.
Qur'an 3:4 and 99:7–8 quoted from Pickthall 1930; confirm exact wording and the parentheses in 3:4.
Al-Muntaqim is in the traditional (Tirmidhi) list; the Qur'an has 'dhu intiqam' (3:4) and 'muntaqimun' (e.g. 32:22). Confirm the trapdoor wording.

Amira arc (1555–1568), day 1: the coffee shop mural she and Jordan painted (arc of 1485–1498) is tagged overnight; Yusuf shrugs, Amira wants payback. The arc runs through the camera footage (a 13-year-old neighbor, Eli), his mom bringing him by, an apology, a fair repair (Eli helps repaint), the repaint Saturday with neighbors and Dadi's food, a rained-out second day, Eli's sketchbook, Jordan's grandmother at the lit wall (the unity beat, 1567), and Amira guiding Eli toward an art program (1568). Paced slowly; no overnight turnarounds.
